lead: With 95% of votes counted, the ANC sits near 31% nationally and the DA near 24%, with hung councils across the country and the MK Party ahead in eThekwini. The IEC is due to declare official results on Sunday; the Springboks face Italy in Turin today.

items.title: ANC on about 31% with 95% of local election votes counted
items.summary: The ANC remains the largest party nationally at roughly 31.2%, down sharply from 2021, while the DA trails on about 24.4%. Many councils will be hung, and the IEC plans to publish seat allocations for all 257 municipalities this weekend.

items.title: DA leads five metros as count nears completion; ANC ahead only in Buffalo City and Mangaung
items.summary: By Friday evening the DA led Johannesburg (38.8%), Tshwane, Ekurhuleni and Nelson Mandela Bay and held Cape Town outright on about 59%. The ANC led Buffalo City and edged the DA by a fraction in Mangaung.

items.title: MK Party ahead in eThekwini on about 40%, but short of a majority
items.summary: MK led the Durban metro with just over 40% on Friday night, so coalition talks will decide who governs. The DA's Haniff Hoosen ruled out working with MK, MK said the same of the DA, and the ANC and EFF say it is too early to talk.

items.title: MK takes four KZN municipalities from the ANC
items.summary: With about 90% of KZN results verified, MK has won control of Richmond outright and leads in Impendle, uMshwathi and Johannes Phumani Phungula, all previously ANC-run. It leads 14 more councils without a majority, while the IFP holds an outright win only in Mthonjaneni.

items.title: Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla loses bid to have July 2021 unrest charges dropped
items.summary: The KwaZulu-Natal High Court in Durban refused her discharge application, so her trial on incitement to terrorism and public violence continues. The case returns to court on 17 May 2027 for arguments.

items.title: ANC elections head doubts a Johannesburg deal that could make Zille mayor
items.summary: Mdumiseni Ntuli said parts of the ANC would resist backing the DA after a bruising campaign, floated sitting in opposition in some councils, and pointed to the party's working relationship with ActionSA in Tshwane.

items.title: DA's Hill-Lewis braces for tough Gauteng coalition negotiations
items.summary: With Cape Town secured, the DA leader says the party now turns to metros in other provinces and expects intense bargaining in the coming days.

items.title: Free helpline for victims of cybercrime launches in South Africa
items.summary: A 12-month pilot run by UK charity The Cyber Helpline offers anonymous step-by-step guidance via a 24-hour chatbot, with tougher cases passed to local responders. Investment scams are the most common problem it expects to handle.

items.title: Democrats take both houses of the US Congress
items.summary: Democrats held about 253 House seats on Friday and 54 Senate seats after flipping seven, with Alaska and Mississippi Senate races still too close to call.

items.title: Trump names Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff
items.summary: Miller, architect of the administration's hardline immigration policies, replaces Susie Wiles from Monday. Democrats are expected to investigate him once they take over Congress in January.

items.title: Tensions stay high in the Strait of Hormuz as Qatar urges a US-Iran deal
items.summary: Iran says it downed a US drone and reports tankers hit in the strait, while Tehran sent a new proposal through Qatari mediators. Qatar's prime minister urged both sides not to wait for a perfect moment to make peace.

items.title: Paraguay's president removed and arrested after bank collapse
items.summary: The Senate voted 44-0 to remove Santiago Pena after the seizure of Ueno Bank cut millions off from their accounts. Vice-president Pedro Alliana was sworn in, and Pena was reportedly detained at home.

items.title: Tanzania's Tundu Lissu cleared of treason but convicted of incitement
items.summary: The High Court in Dar es Salaam acquitted the Chadema chairman of treason, which can carry the death penalty, but found him guilty of the lesser charge of incitement.

items.title: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie jailed for 200 years
items.summary: A Mombasa court sentenced the Shakahola church leader over the deaths of 190 children and an adult, and jailed 28 accomplices. Authorities say more than 400 people died in the tragedy.

items.title: JSE gains 6.7% in a week as foreign money returns
items.summary: South Africa's main share index rose sharply over the week, far outpacing emerging-market peers, which slipped. The rand traded near R16.52 to the dollar on Friday.

items.title: Rand eases as a global AI selloff lifts the dollar
items.summary: The rand slipped about 0.3% to around R16.53 on Friday morning and the 2035 bond yield rose to 8.33% as investors sought safety; economists say stable post-election city governments are what markets will watch.

items.title: Wall Street steadies after its worst AI-driven week since June
items.summary: The Nasdaq rose 1.1% and the S&P 500 0.3% on Friday after a sharp tech selloff, while the US added 165,000 jobs in October, well above forecasts.

items.title: Week ahead: SA jobless figures on Tuesday, SARB decision on 19 November
items.summary: Third-quarter unemployment data is due 10 November after October's PMI came in at 49, below forecast. The Reserve Bank's next rate decision follows on 19 November, with the repo rate at 7.25%.

items.title: Springboks face Italy in Turin today
items.summary: Siya Kolisi's side meet Italy at the Allianz Stadium at 13:40 SA time in the Nations Championship, with Salmaan Moerat back at lock. France in Paris and Ireland in Dublin follow later this month.

items.title: Chiefs seek Carling Knockout lift against Siwelele
items.summary: Under-pressure coach Da Cruz takes Kaizer Chiefs to Polokwane for Sunday's 6pm quarterfinal after one win in seven and last weekend's 2-1 Soweto derby defeat to Pirates.

items.title: Mosimane names 27-man Bafana squad for Kenya double-header
items.summary: Bafana Bafana, top of AFCON qualifying Group D, host Benni McCarthy's Kenya at Orlando Stadium before the return leg in Kenya. Mbekezeli Mbokazi and Lyle Foster are among those recalled.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football
items.summary: The 41-year-old leaves Portugal with men's records of 234 caps and 146 goals, announcing his exit online after being left out by coach Jorge Jesus.

items.title: EU tells TikTok to fix its For You feed or face fines
items.summary: The European Commission says the feed's 'rabbit hole' effect breaches the Digital Services Act and could fine TikTok up to 6% of turnover. TikTok calls the findings inaccurate.

items.title: Protesters occupy Microsoft data centre site in Amsterdam
items.summary: Hundreds entered the construction site as part of Europe-wide protests over the energy and water demands of AI data centres; Dutch police detained up to 200 people.

items.title: US measles cases pass 5,000, the most since 1991
items.summary: The CDC has confirmed 5,182 cases this year, more than double 2025's total, with most in children and teenagers and kindergarten vaccination rates falling.
